reference_traces.rationale: The final paper retains the reported extension of automated analysis to one-, two-, and three-color data and to state-transition analysis, matching the reviewer’s description of the contribution.

The response describes additional comparisons but explicitly notes that a direct DeepFRET comparison was not included; the final paper reports a comparison with published routines without fully isolating relative performance across automated packages.
The reviewer’s account of the DNN package and its simulation and experimental evaluation is retained in the final article’s stated workflow and benchmarks.
The final paper documents comparisons across noise levels and local and global HMM settings, consistent with the reviewer’s positive appraisal of the evaluation.
The final paper retains the reviewer-noted potential to improve reproducibility and reduce multi-color analysis complexity through automated classification and calibration.

The authors added independently trained networks and a consistency analysis, but the final paper still conditions reliability on representative training data and calls for independent validation on new datasets.

The response adds noisy protein examples and discusses their classification, but the final paper continues to identify low-SNR operation as a limit and states that high-threshold analysis discards most poor-SNR traces.

The response says that supplementary material now provides architecture and parameter details, while the final paper’s main workflow description does not itself state the loss-function and default-parameter rationale requested by the reviewer.

The added discussion labels neural-network outputs as artificial confidence levels and acknowledges limits of interpretability, but it does not show their calibration against probabilistic confidence from explicit models.
The requested qualification of the temperature explanation was addressed through added temperature measurements and retained final discussion; this is audit-only.
The final paper compares local and global HMM settings, and the subsequent reviewer report finds the comparison fair; this is audit-only.
The final article provides both program and documentation links; this is audit-only.
The final workflow specifies the FRET corrections, so the requested clarification is audit-only.

limiting_points.suggested_action: State the scope and basis of comparisons with existing automated smFRET analysis packages.
limiting_points.text: The relative advantage over established automated software remains incompletely isolated because the final comparison is not a standardized head-to-head evaluation across packages.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Specify the extension beyond prior deep-learning classifiers and conventional kinetic-analysis workflows.
supporting_points.text: Deep-LASI extends automated single-molecule analysis to one-, two-, and three-color data while integrating trace sorting, FRET correction, state assignment, and kinetic extraction.

questions.suggested_action: Document the loss function, default hyperparameters, and their selection rationale alongside the stated architecture.
questions.text: What loss function and default-parameter rationale govern the CNN-LSTM classifiers, beyond the high-level architecture description?

questions.suggested_action: Explain how reported neural-network confidence outputs are calibrated and how they should be interpreted relative to model-based posterior probabilities.
questions.text: How should the classifier confidence outputs be calibrated and interpreted relative to posterior probabilities from explicit emission models?

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the integrated description of trace classification, correction, and kinetic analysis across imaging modalities.
strengths.text: The work presents an integrated DNN workflow for rapid analysis of single-molecule traces and evaluates it with simulations, manual analyses, HMM analysis, and experimental applications.

strengths.suggested_action: Maintain the explicit local-versus-global HMM and manual-versus-automated comparisons.
strengths.text: The evaluation examines performance over noise, state separation, and dynamic timescales, and directly tests local and global HMM comparisons as well as manual selection.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the evidence linking automated classification to reproducibility, correction-factor estimation, and protein-data analysis.
strengths.text: Deep-LASI demonstrates reproducible analysis across independently trained networks, automated derivation of correction factors, and agreement with manually evaluated protein data.

summary.text: Deep-LASI provides an integrated CNN-LSTM workflow for classifying and analyzing one-, two-, and three-color single-molecule data, with benchmarks against manual and HMM analyses and applications to DNA origami, protein, and confocal data. The study’s extension to multicolor kinetic analysis is a substantive contribution. Its remaining limits concern relative comparison with established automated software, dependence on representative simulated training data, and constrained performance on poor-SNR traces. Residual methodological questions concern parameter documentation and calibration of neural-network confidence outputs.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Report validation on independent experimental datasets that differ materially from the simulated training distribution and define the supported operating domain.
weaknesses.text: Although independently generated training sets were compared, reliability and generalizability remain dependent on the representativeness and quality of the training data.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify selection, false-positive, and false-negative behavior across poor-SNR regimes and report how confidence-threshold choices affect conclusions.
weaknesses.text: For low-SNR data, the high-confidence default discards most traces, leaving performance and selection bias at the practical operating limit incompletely quantified.
